(2) SECURITY -- EUR2.7B revenue, crossed Q1 cash-flow breakeven 'for the first time in a first quarter', US double-digit, Cipher cyber folded in to reposition as integrated physical+digital security. bear_thesis: Prosegur is a structurally low-quality, FX-cursed, low-margin manned-guarding conglomerate that DESERVES its discount and has NO catalyst to close it. # Prosegur Compañía de Seguridad, S.A. (PSG.MC) — Forensic Dossier

*Interrogator dossier (Claude Opus 4.8). Source: Prosegur FY2025 results & press release (prosegur.com); Q4-2025 and Q1-2026 earnings calls/slides (Investing.com transcripts); company IR; CNMV history (Gubel tender offer). No FMP transcript was bundled; this dossier reasons from the screener financial trajectory cross-referenced against the most recent management commentary found on the web. Quotes are management phrasings reported in the Q1-2026 / Q4-2025 call coverage; numbers from the screener block are labeled (financials). Latest hard quarter: Q1 FY2026 (ended 31-Mar-2026).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Prosegur is a three-engine physical-security conglomerate — **Security** (manned guarding + tech), **Cash** (cash-in-transit and cash management, held via the ~74% owned listed subsidiary Prosegur Cash, CASH.MC), and **Alarms** (residential/SME monitoring). The story management has told across the last several quarters is consistent and, unusually for a deep-value name, *improving*: a multi-year "value creation for shareholders" deleveraging-and-margin-recovery arc.

The arc's evolution: the older narrative was dominated by **LatAm FX as an existential drag** masking real volume growth. By FY2025 the framing shifted to "**organic growth is the truth, FX is noise**" — management leads every release with organic figures (FY2025 organic +10%, Q1-2026 organic +7.8%) and treats the reported number (FY2025 +0.5%, Q1-2026 +1.5%) as a translation artifact. The newest thread, introduced in Q1-2026, is **structural margin transformation**: in Cash, "transformation products now represent 36.4% of total Cash sales" (recurring, higher-margin services replacing volume-linked CIT); in Alarms, a deliberate pivot from "grow the base at any cost" to "**quality growth**" (churn cut from 95bps to 67bps, service margin 21%→25%). The Security narrative crossed a symbolic line in Q1-2026: "**Security reached cash flow breakeven for the first time in a first quarter**," and Cipher cybersecurity was folded into Security to sell "integrated physical and digital security."

Growth drivers quietly dropped: the old emphasis on top-line CIT volume in Cash is replaced by "transformation products" — a tacit admission that legacy cash logistics is ex-growth and the bet is mix-shift to services. Drivers added: US Security double-digit growth, Alarms unit economics, and balance-sheet deleveraging as the headline value driver.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The hard evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong, broad-based growth" | Reported revenue FY2025 +0.5%, Q1-2026 +1.5% (financials/web). 3-yr CAGR +5.7%. Organic +10% / +7.8%. | **Half-true.** Organic strength is genuine; reported is near-zero because FX (ARS/USD) erases it. A shareholder is paid in reported euros, not organic. |
| "On the right track… generating value for shareholders" — earnings inflection | Net income €78M (2024) → €119M (2025), +52.8% (web/financials). EPS €0.15 → €0.22, +46.7% YoY. EBITA €357M, +8.9%. | **TRUE and material.** The load-bearing fact. Earnings power inflects hard while revenue is flat — operating leverage + tax-rate normalization (effective tax 42.0%, −449bps YoY). |
| Margin expansion | Net margin 2.4% (financials); gross 20.4% stable; consolidated EBITDA margin 11.1%, EBITA ~6.8%. Security EBITA margin 2.8%. | **Mixed.** Group margin is structurally thin (manned guarding is a 2–3% EBIT business). Expansion is real at the EBITA line (+8.9%) but off a low base; net margin remains razor-thin. |
| Deleveraging | Net debt €1.62B (financials, 2026-03-31); group reported €1.381B; Net debt/EBITDA 2.4x, −€28M QoQ; target <2.4x by year-end. | **TRUE, slow.** Deleveraging is happening at a modest pace; €1.6B net debt against €119M net income is still heavy leverage. |
| FCF recovery | TTM FCF €218M (financials); P/FCF 5.5x; FCF +53.3% YoY; Q1-2026 operating cash flow +€8M vs −€19M prior-year (web). | **TRUE.** Second load-bearing fact — FCF is real, growing, and 5.5x is genuinely cheap if sustainable. Q1 turning cash-positive is a structural seasonality break. |

Where the story is **richer than the numbers**: "value creation" framing implies a re-rating is owed; nothing in the reported top line (flat) supports a growth re-rate — only the earnings/FCF inflection does. Where it's **poorer**: management undersells how much of the EPS jump is tax-rate + operating leverage rather than demand, and how exposed it is to one more ARS devaluation.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising / Stable (confident, not defensive).** Across Q4-2025 and Q1-2026 the tone is offensive: "a strong first quarter," "solid operations performance," "broad-based growth across regions," "on the right track to comply with our main objective." Management volunteers point forward revenue figures (Q2 €1.44B, Q3 €1.49B) — a confidence tell; ex-growth managements give ranges, not points. Language is *operational and granular* (churn bps, transformation-product %, DSO) rather than macro-excuse-laden, a green flag for a LatAm-exposed name. The one defensive note is FX, handled with "robust risk management practices" but no quantified hedge disclosure.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium-High.** Financials show beats in 5 of 7 quarters (71%, financials) and FY2025 net profit "exceeding targets" (company headline). EPS delivery compounded +22.4% over 3 years and the +52.8% net-profit jump beat the company's own FY2025 objective. Management gives point revenue forecasts and broadly delivers — Q1-2026 net profit +15.2% continues the streak. The reliability gap is FX: management cannot guide reported numbers credibly (they don't control the peso), so they shifted goalposts to organic + earnings, where they deliver. **Score: Medium-High** on what they control; Low on reported-euro predictability.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

(1) **FX/earnings sensitivity** — pressed for quantified FX impact, management offered "robust risk management practices" with no hedge ratios (a non-answer). (2) **Security margin sustainability** — pushed on whether 2.8% EBITA keeps climbing, the CFO conceded improvements "will be less significant over the course of the year" — the easy margin gains are behind. (3) **Cash/Argentina** — Cash EBITA flat, "negatively impacted by Argentina macroeconomic conditions," the structural soft underbelly. What analysts are NOT pushing on but should: the absence of any catalyst to close the holdco/SoP discount (no buyback ramp, no Cash take-private, no asset sale).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 Net income +52.8% FY2025, EPS +46.7% — a genuine earnings inflection, not engineering (corroborated by EBITA +8.9% + tax normalization).
🟢 FCF €218M TTM at 5.5x P/FCF; Q1-2026 turned operating-cash-positive (+€8M vs −€19M).
🟢 Alarms unit economics improving (churn 95→67bps, service margin 21%→25%).
🟢 Deleveraging on track (2.4x, −€28M QoQ), BBB rated, 60%+ debt fixed at 2.9% avg cost.
🔴 Net margin 2.4%, Security EBITA margin 2.8%, ROIC 3.7% (financials) — structurally low quality; the business *deserves* a discount.
🔴 Reported revenue flat (+0.5% FY, +1.5% Q1) — the growth story lives in "organic," which FX repeatedly eats.
🔴 €1.6B net debt is heavy; Argentina/ARS is a recurring, uncontrollable hit to Cash.
🔴 **No catalyst.** The only structural event — Gubel's €1.83/share tender — closed March 2024 *below* today's €2.68. No live buyback ramp, no Cash take-private, no asset sale, no activist. Insider buy ratio 0.00 (financials).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The terminology shift from "volume" to "**transformation products**" in Cash is the key tell — it concedes legacy CIT is in secular decline and reframes the bet as a services/mix story (margin over volume). The Cipher-into-Security integration signals Prosegur wants to be sold as an *integrated* security platform, not a labor-arbitrage guard company — a multiple-aspiration move, though the 2.8% margin says the market won't pay for it yet. The ritual invocation of "value for shareholders" without any accompanying capital-return action (flat ~€0.13/sh dividend, ~4.9% yield, no buyback acceleration) reads as aspiration, not plan — management knows the stock is cheap and is signaling, but holds no forcing function.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**STRENGTHENING (operationally) / STABLE (structurally).** The operating trajectory is genuinely improving — earnings, FCF, Alarms economics, deleveraging all point the right way, and management is credible and confident on what it controls. But this is a *quality-improving-but-still-low-quality* compounder with **no catalyst to force the discount closed**. The single most important thing the director must weigh: **this is a pure margin-of-safety / FCF-multiple bet, not a special situation.** The €1.83 Gubel tender already fired (below today's price), Gubel already owns ~75%, and there is no announced buyback ramp, Cash take-private, or asset sale to act as a forcing function. You are paid 5.5x FCF and a ~4.9% dividend to wait for a re-rate that has no dated trigger and is perpetually one ARS devaluation away from being erased on the reported line.

# Prosegur Compañía de Seguridad, S.A. (PSG.MC) — Forensic Dossier

*Interrogator dossier (Claude Opus 4.8). Source: Prosegur FY2025 results & press release (prosegur.com); Q4-2025 and Q1-2026 earnings calls/slides (Investing.com transcripts); company IR; CNMV history (Gubel tender offer). No FMP transcript was bundled; this dossier reasons from the screener financial trajectory cross-referenced against the most recent management commentary found on the web. Quotes are management phrasings reported in the Q1-2026 / Q4-2025 call coverage; numbers from the screener block are labeled (financials). Latest hard quarter: Q1 FY2026 (ended 31-Mar-2026).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Prosegur is a three-engine physical-security conglomerate — **Security** (manned guarding + tech), **Cash** (cash-in-transit and cash management, held via the ~74% owned listed subsidiary Prosegur Cash, CASH.MC), and **Alarms** (residential/SME monitoring). The story management has told across the last several quarters is consistent and, unusually for a deep-value name, *improving*: a multi-year "value creation for shareholders" deleveraging-and-margin-recovery arc.

The arc's evolution: the older narrative was dominated by **LatAm FX as an existential drag** masking real volume growth. By FY2025 the framing shifted to "**organic growth is the truth, FX is noise**" — management leads every release with organic figures (FY2025 organic +10%, Q1-2026 organic +7.8%) and treats the reported number (FY2025 +0.5%, Q1-2026 +1.5%) as a translation artifact. The newest thread, introduced in Q1-2026, is **structural margin transformation**: in Cash, "transformation products now represent 36.4% of total Cash sales" (recurring, higher-margin services replacing volume-linked CIT); in Alarms, a deliberate pivot from "grow the base at any cost" to "**quality growth**" (churn cut from 95bps to 67bps, service margin 21%→25%). The Security narrative crossed a symbolic line in Q1-2026: "**Security reached cash flow breakeven for the first time in a first quarter**," and Cipher cybersecurity was folded into Security to sell "integrated physical and digital security."

Growth drivers quietly dropped: the old emphasis on top-line CIT volume in Cash is replaced by "transformation products" — a tacit admission that legacy cash logistics is ex-growth and the bet is mix-shift to services. Drivers added: US Security double-digit growth, Alarms unit economics, and balance-sheet deleveraging as the headline value driver.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The hard evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong, broad-based growth" | Reported revenue FY2025 +0.5%, Q1-2026 +1.5% (financials/web). 3-yr CAGR +5.7%. Organic +10% / +7.8%. | **Half-true.** Organic strength is genuine; reported is near-zero because FX (ARS/USD) erases it. A shareholder is paid in reported euros, not organic. |
| "On the right track… generating value for shareholders" — earnings inflection | Net income €78M (2024) → €119M (2025), +52.8% (web/financials). EPS €0.15 → €0.22, +46.7% YoY. EBITA €357M, +8.9%. | **TRUE and material.** The load-bearing fact. Earnings power inflects hard while revenue is flat — operating leverage + tax-rate normalization (effective tax 42.0%, −449bps YoY). |
| Margin expansion | Net margin 2.4% (financials); gross 20.4% stable; consolidated EBITDA margin 11.1%, EBITA ~6.8%. Security EBITA margin 2.8%. | **Mixed.** Group margin is structurally thin (manned guarding is a 2–3% EBIT business). Expansion is real at the EBITA line (+8.9%) but off a low base; net margin remains razor-thin. |
| Deleveraging | Net debt €1.62B (financials, 2026-03-31); group reported €1.381B; Net debt/EBITDA 2.4x, −€28M QoQ; target <2.4x by year-end. | **TRUE, slow.** Deleveraging is happening at a modest pace; €1.6B net debt against €119M net income is still heavy leverage. |
| FCF recovery | TTM FCF €218M (financials); P/FCF 5.5x; FCF +53.3% YoY; Q1-2026 operating cash flow +€8M vs −€19M prior-year (web). | **TRUE.** Second load-bearing fact — FCF is real, growing, and 5.5x is genuinely cheap if sustainable. Q1 turning cash-positive is a structural seasonality break. |

Where the story is **richer than the numbers**: "value creation" framing implies a re-rating is owed; nothing in the reported top line (flat) supports a growth re-rate — only the earnings/FCF inflection does. Where it's **poorer**: management undersells how much of the EPS jump is tax-rate + operating leverage rather than demand, and how exposed it is to one more ARS devaluation.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising / Stable (confident, not defensive).** Across Q4-2025 and Q1-2026 the tone is offensive: "a strong first quarter," "solid operations performance," "broad-based growth across regions," "on the right track to comply with our main objective." Management volunteers point forward revenue figures (Q2 €1.44B, Q3 €1.49B) — a confidence tell; ex-growth managements give ranges, not points. Language is *operational and granular* (churn bps, transformation-product %, DSO) rather than macro-excuse-laden, a green flag for a LatAm-exposed name. The one defensive note is FX, handled with "robust risk management practices" but no quantified hedge disclosure.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium-High.** Financials show beats in 5 of 7 quarters (71%, financials) and FY2025 net profit "exceeding targets" (company headline). EPS delivery compounded +22.4% over 3 years and the +52.8% net-profit jump beat the company's own FY2025 objective. Management gives point revenue forecasts and broadly delivers — Q1-2026 net profit +15.2% continues the streak. The reliability gap is FX: management cannot guide reported numbers credibly (they don't control the peso), so they shifted goalposts to organic + earnings, where they deliver. **Score: Medium-High** on what they control; Low on reported-euro predictability.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

(1) **FX/earnings sensitivity** — pressed for quantified FX impact, management offered "robust risk management practices" with no hedge ratios (a non-answer). (2) **Security margin sustainability** — pushed on whether 2.8% EBITA keeps climbing, the CFO conceded improvements "will be less significant over the course of the year" — the easy margin gains are behind. (3) **Cash/Argentina** — Cash EBITA flat, "negatively impacted by Argentina macroeconomic conditions," the structural soft underbelly. What analysts are NOT pushing on but should: the absence of any catalyst to close the holdco/SoP discount (no buyback ramp, no Cash take-private, no asset sale).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 Net income +52.8% FY2025, EPS +46.7% — a genuine earnings inflection, not engineering (corroborated by EBITA +8.9% + tax normalization).
🟢 FCF €218M TTM at 5.5x P/FCF; Q1-2026 turned operating-cash-positive (+€8M vs −€19M).
🟢 Alarms unit economics improving (churn 95→67bps, service margin 21%→25%).
🟢 Deleveraging on track (2.4x, −€28M QoQ), BBB rated, 60%+ debt fixed at 2.9% avg cost.
🔴 Net margin 2.4%, Security EBITA margin 2.8%, ROIC 3.7% (financials) — structurally low quality; the business *deserves* a discount.
🔴 Reported revenue flat (+0.5% FY, +1.5% Q1) — the growth story lives in "organic," which FX repeatedly eats.
🔴 €1.6B net debt is heavy; Argentina/ARS is a recurring, uncontrollable hit to Cash.
🔴 **No catalyst.** The only structural event — Gubel's €1.83/share tender — closed March 2024 *below* today's €2.68. No live buyback ramp, no Cash take-private, no asset sale, no activist. Insider buy ratio 0.00 (financials).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The terminology shift from "volume" to "**transformation products**" in Cash is the key tell — it concedes legacy CIT is in secular decline and reframes the bet as a services/mix story (margin over volume). The Cipher-into-Security integration signals Prosegur wants to be sold as an *integrated* security platform, not a labor-arbitrage guard company — a multiple-aspiration move, though the 2.8% margin says the market won't pay for it yet. The ritual invocation of "value for shareholders" without any accompanying capital-return action (flat ~€0.13/sh dividend, ~4.9% yield, no buyback acceleration) reads as aspiration, not plan — management knows the stock is cheap and is signaling, but holds no forcing function.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**STRENGTHENING (operationally) / STABLE (structurally).** The operating trajectory is genuinely improving — earnings, FCF, Alarms economics, deleveraging all point the right way, and management is credible and confident on what it controls. But this is a *quality-improving-but-still-low-quality* compounder with **no catalyst to force the discount closed**. The single most important thing the director must weigh: **this is a pure margin-of-safety / FCF-multiple bet, not a special situation.** The €1.83 Gubel tender already fired (below today's price), Gubel already owns ~75%, and there is no announced buyback ramp, Cash take-private, or asset sale to act as a forcing function. You are paid 5.5x FCF and a ~4.9% dividend to wait for a re-rate that has no dated trigger and is perpetually one ARS devaluation away from being erased on the reported line.

CREDIBILITY_SCORE: 4 | TRAJECTORY: STRENGTHENING

bull_thesis: Prosegur is a Madrid-listed holding company, and the bull case is a classic sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately) argument: the pieces are worth more than the whole trades for, and management is finally trying to close that gap. The company owns three things. First, a roughly 72% controlling stake in Prosegur Cash, a separately listed cash-logistics company that the market prices at about €933M — so the stake alone is worth on the order of €670M, an objective, market-set anchor rather than a guess. Second, a manned-guarding and technology security arm (Prosegur Security) that did about €2.6B of revenue in 2025 with operating profit (EBITA) up 10.7% to €90M and margins expanding. Third, and most interesting, a fast-growing residential-alarms business run as a joint venture with Telefonica (Movistar Prosegur Alarmas) that the chief financial officer has openly called 'the hidden treasury of Prosegur' — a recurring-subscription business with about 1.1M clients and real switching costs, the kind of asset that fetched a rich price when rival Verisure listed. The operating momentum is genuine and improving: 2025 net income jumped 53% to €119M, free cash flow rose 53%, and the first quarter of 2026 swung to positive operating cash flow (€8M versus negative €19M a year earlier) with profit up 15%. Underlying organic growth (stripping out currency) ran about 8-10%, far ahead of the flat reported line, which is depressed almost entirely by the weak Argentine peso and U.S. dollar against the euro. Management has scheduled a dedicated Alarms investor day for December 2026 to make the value-surfacing case, and has nudged the dividend up 3.6%. If the market re-rates the Alarms business toward its recurring-revenue peers and credits the Cash stake at fair value, the equity is worth meaningfully more than today's price. Conditions the bull case needs: the December event has to produce a credible path to crystallizing Alarms value (a listing, stake sale, or clean spin), the Alarms churn spike must normalize as promised, and currency must stop erasing the organic growth.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that there is simply no discount to arbitrage here — the market is already paying a full sum-of-the-parts price — and the catalyst everyone is waiting for is soft and has been explicitly deferred. Start with valuation: at about €2.83 the stock carries a €1.51B market value; a fair sum-of-the-parts (the listed Cash stake at its market price, Security at a manned-guarding peer multiple, the alarms economic interest at a recurring-revenue multiple, less roughly €0.9-1.0B of holding-company-level net debt) lands right around €2.40 per share — below, not above, the current price. The screener's own models agree: fair value €2.40, discounted-cash-flow value €2.0, a margin of safety of about -8%, and cash-flow-based methods (discounted cash flow -40%, earnings-power value -21%) all say the stock is fully priced to slightly expensive. The peer read agrees too: against Loomis (the closest cash-in-transit pure-play, on an EV/EBITDA of roughly 6x) and Securitas, Prosegur screens 'in line,' not cheap. This is a low-quality earnings base — net margin about 2.4%, return on invested capital about 3.7%, well below the cost of capital — dressed up by a one-year profit inflection. The load-bearing catalyst is weak: the December Alarms investor day is a strategy presentation, not a binding transaction, and management has said outright that an Alarms IPO or spin is 'not on the table' in the short term even after Verisure's successful listing. Worse, the Spanish alarms business is a 50/50 joint venture with Telefonica, so Prosegur cannot cleanly crystallize it alone — any separation needs a partner's assent. Meanwhile the near-term operating picture deteriorated first: first-quarter 2026 alarms churn rose to 13% and recurring cash flow fell about 10% as the new 'quality growth' model bit, and free cash flow was seasonally negative €32M. And the whole structure carries about €1.62B of net debt sitting ahead of the equity. What confirms the bear: a December event that offers strategy but no crystallization path, churn that fails to normalize, and continued currency erosion of the organic story.
consensus_delta: For a deep-value name the question is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into a company with stable-to-growing earnings power. Here it largely is not — and that is the problem. The market is already crediting the 2025 profit inflection (net income +53%, free cash flow +53%) and paying a full sum-of-the-parts price of about €2.83, slightly above a reasonable €2.40 base-case fair value. There is no meaningful holding-company discount left to arbitrage: the peer read is 'in line,' cash-flow-based valuation methods say the stock is fully-to-over-priced, and the listed Prosegur Cash stake gives the market an objective anchor it is already using. The only place where we might disagree with the street is the alarms business — if the December 2026 investor day genuinely re-rates it toward recurring-subscription peers, there is a case the market under-credits that one part. But that is a narrow, event-contingent disagreement, not a broad mispricing, and it is diluted by the fact that the Spanish alarms operation is a 50/50 joint venture with Telefonica that Prosegur cannot crystallize on its own.
forcing_function: The load-bearing catalyst is the December 2026 Alarms investor day, and it is soft and non-binding rather than a hard, dated transaction. Management has publicly framed the alarms arm as 'the hidden treasury' and set up the December event to make the value-surfacing case — but it has also said, as recently as early 2026 and even after Verisure's successful listing, that an alarms IPO or spin is 'not on the table' in the short term. So the event is a strategy presentation that may or may not lay out a crystallization path; it is not a contractual payout, a fixed deal, or a dated corporate action. Compounding this, the Spanish alarms business is a 50/50 joint venture with Telefonica, so no clean separation can happen without a partner's agreement. This is a serially-deferred, single-binary catalyst with no firm trigger — the weakest kind — and it does not force a re-rating.
valley_of_death: The near-term (next three to nine months) risks are real but not catastrophic. First, currency: a Latin-America-weighted revenue base means the weak Argentine peso and U.S. dollar can keep erasing the 8-10% organic growth in the reported euro line, as they did in both 2025 and the first quarter of 2026 — quarters can look flat-to-poor on the headline even when the business is growing. Second, alarms execution: churn rose to 13% in the first quarter of 2026 and recurring cash flow fell about 10% as the new stricter-credit 'quality growth' model took hold; if churn fails to normalize toward 9-10% by year-end as promised, the 'hidden treasury' narrative weakens right before the December event meant to showcase it. Third, seasonality and leverage: first-quarter free cash flow was negative €32M and the group carries about €1.62B of net debt at 2.4x operating profit — manageable, but it leaves little room for disappointment. None of these is a solvency threat, but each can punish the stock before any value-surfacing catalyst arrives.
positioning_washout: There is no obvious forced- or mechanical-selling dynamic to exploit. Prosegur is a founder-and-family-controlled holding company with a stable, non-yield-chasing shareholder base, so there is no dividend-cut or index-driven flush waiting to clear out weak holders and create a cheap entry. The dividend was actually nudged up 3.6%. That absence of a washout cuts both ways: it means less downside from mechanical selling, but it also means there is no forced-seller dislocation to buy into — one of the fatter special-situation lanes in the current regime, and it is simply not present here.
moderator_conclusion: This is a pass for now. Prosegur is a decent, improving business — profit and cash flow genuinely inflected in 2025, and the holding-company structure (a market-priced 72% Prosegur Cash stake, a low-margin but growing Security arm, and a promising alarms joint venture) is exactly the kind of setup where a sum-of-the-parts discount can pay off. The trouble is that the discount is not there: at about €2.83 the stock already trades at or slightly above a reasonable base-case sum-of-the-parts of ~€2.40, the peer read is 'in line' rather than cheap, and cash-flow-based valuation methods say it is fully to modestly over-priced. The value case is respectable on its own terms — hence a middling value grade — but it is not a bargain, and an eroding-quality caveat applies: returns on capital in the low single digits sit below the cost of capital, so this is a thin-margin base, not a compounding one. The current market regime rewards hard-dated special situations — forced-seller and spin windows are the fattest lane right now — and penalizes soft, deferred, single-binary catalysts. Prosegur's only real catalyst, the December 2026 Alarms investor day, is precisely the deferred, non-binding kind the regime tells us to avoid: management has said an alarms listing is 'not on the table' short-term, and the Spanish alarms business is a 50/50 Telefonica joint venture that cannot be crystallized unilaterally. There is no forced-selling dislocation to buy into either. The risk-reward is unattractive — roughly -15% to base-case fair value and about -38% to the adverse case, against maybe +10% of catalyst-contingent upside. Better to pass and revisit only if the December event produces a concrete, dated crystallization path, or if the stock washes out well below €2.40 and re-opens a genuine margin of safety.
sop_breakdown: Base-case sum-of-the-parts ≈ €2.40 per share, blending the two cases. Contributions: the 72% Prosegur Cash stake at roughly its market value adds about €1.25/share; Prosegur Security at ~9-10x operating profit adds about €1.55/share; the alarms economic interest adds about €1.00/share; added-value outsourcing, cyber and other add about €0.25/share — gross parts ~€3.85 add up to ~€2,050M, from which about €0.90B (~€1.70/share) of holding-company-level net debt is subtracted (Prosegur Cash's own debt is excluded because it already sits inside the Cash market value). Net equity ≈ €1.28B across 532.7M shares ≈ €2.40 per share — essentially identical to the screener's €2.40 fair value and Buffett value, and just below the ~€2.83 current price.
risk_reward: Poor-to-neutral. Upside to base-case fair value of ~€2.40 is negative from the ~€2.83 price (roughly -15%); the bull sum-of-the-parts of ~€3.10 is only ~+10% and requires a full alarms re-rating that has no binding trigger. Downside to the adverse sum-of-the-parts of ~€1.75 is about -38%. The asymmetry points the wrong way: limited, catalyst-dependent upside against a real fundamental-value floor well below today's price.
peer_comps_note: The provided peer group (Loomis, Securitas, plus SIS.MI and G4S-type security services) and the 'in_line' verdict are decisive here and treated as an independent relative-value check. Prosegur screens roughly fairly priced, not cheap, versus Loomis (the closest cash-in-transit pure-play, on an EV/EBITDA of about 6x as of spring 2026) and Securitas. Its optical cheapness on some accounting-based methods (Graham +74%, owner-earnings +31%) is offset by expensiveness on cash-flow-based methods (discounted cash flow -40%, earnings-power value -21%), which the peer note attributes to genuine margin thinness in the cash-in-transit segment. Critically, the shared secular driver — the slow decline of physical cash usage — is a sector-wide factor that de-rates Loomis and Prosegur's Cash segment together; the discount to that peer is shared-factor sector beta, not name-specific edge, so it earns no idiosyncratic-alpha credit. The alarms business is the one part where Prosegur may carry a peer-relative asset the cash-in-transit comps do not, but its value is muddied by the 50/50 Telefonica joint venture.

# Forensic Dossier — Prosegur Compañía de Seguridad (PSG.MC)

*A deep dive on management and the setup. No earnings-call transcript was bundled with this name, so this dossier reasons from the most recent public results — the full-year 2025 release (reported 27 February 2026) and the first-quarter 2026 earnings call (reported late April 2026) — cross-referenced against the screener's own financial trajectory. Where a figure comes from those releases rather than the screener, it is flagged.*

Prosegur is not a single business — it is a Madrid-listed holding company that owns three quite different things: a manned-guarding and technology security arm (Prosegur Security), a roughly 72% controlling stake in a separately listed cash-logistics company (Prosegur Cash, ticker CASH.MC), and a fast-growing residential and small-business alarms business (Prosegur Alarms, run as a joint venture branded Movistar Prosegur Alarmas). That structure is the whole story here, and everything below should be read through it.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management is telling has shifted over the last two years from "we are a diversified security services group fighting a currency war" to "we are a holding company sitting on hidden value we intend to surface." Two threads run through the recent commentary.

First, the operating narrative is one of strong underlying growth being masked by foreign-exchange (the movement in currencies like the Argentine peso and the U.S. dollar against the euro). In full-year 2025 the company grew revenue about 10% on an organic basis — that is, stripping out currency and acquisitions — but reported growth of only 0.5%, because a roughly 10% adverse currency swing wiped out nearly all of it. The same pattern repeated in the first quarter of 2026: 8% organic growth collapsed to 1.5% reported. Management leans hard on the organic number and asks investors to look through the currency drag.

Second, and newer, is the "hidden treasury" narrative around the Alarms business. The chief financial officer, Maite Rodríguez Sedano, has explicitly called the alarms arm "the hidden treasury of Prosegur," and the company has scheduled a dedicated Alarms-focused investor day for December 2026 (an event where management lays out strategy and, often, a plan to surface value). This is a meaningful thesis shift: a company that historically presented itself as an integrated security group is now openly flagging that one of its parts is worth more than the market credits, and is holding a set-piece event to make that case.

A quieter third thread: the Alarms growth model itself was re-tooled in early 2026 — away from chasing raw client additions toward "quality growth," with higher upfront fees and stricter credit terms. That is a deliberate near-term slowdown for better long-term unit economics, which management is asking investors to trust.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising.** Across 2025 into early 2026 management moved from defensive currency-explaining to offensive value-surfacing. The full-year 2025 release led with a 44% jump in net profit; the first-quarter 2026 call led with 15% profit growth and a swing to positive operating cash flow (€8M versus negative €19M a year earlier). The scheduling of a dedicated Alarms investor day is itself a confidence signal — companies do not spotlight a segment they intend to keep buried. The one note of defensiveness is around Alarms churn, which management pre-emptively addressed, promising normalization by year-end.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium-to-high.** The screener records a beat on 5 of the last 7 quarters (about 71%), which is a solid, believable delivery record rather than a suspiciously perfect one. Management gave specific forward revenue markers on the first-quarter 2026 call (roughly €1.44B for the second quarter, €1.49B for the third) and specific churn-normalization timing — the willingness to put dated numbers on the table is a credibility positive. The recurring risk to credibility is not honesty but currency: an organic-growth guide can be entirely correct and still miss the reported line if the peso and dollar move against them, which they repeatedly have.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

The pressure points cluster on three things. First, **when and how the Alarms value gets surfaced** — the December investor day is being set up as the answer, which means it is also the moment of maximum disappointment risk if management shows up with a strategy update but no crystallization path. Second, **Alarms churn** — analysts pushed on the jump to 13%, and management's answer (involuntary cancellations from stricter credit terms, normalizing later in the year) is a promise that has to be delivered. Third, **the currency drag** — the perennial "when does the organic story finally show up in reported euros" question, to which there is no satisfying answer while the Latin-American exposure remains.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 Profit and free cash flow genuinely inflected: net income up 53% and free cash flow up 53% in 2025; a swing to positive operating cash flow in the first quarter of 2026.
🟢 A separately listed, liquid Cash stake gives an objective, market-set value for the largest part of the business — the sum-of-the-parts is anchored in a real price, not an assumption.
🟢 Management is actively trying to surface value (the December Alarms day), and modestly raised the dividend (+3.6% to €90M).
🔴 Reported growth is chronically flattered-away by currency; a Latin-America-weighted revenue base means this is structural, not a passing headwind.
🔴 Thin net margin (about 2.4%) and low returns on capital (return on invested capital about 3.7%, per the screener) — this is a low-quality earnings base even after the improvement.
🔴 Alarms churn rose and recurring cash fell as the new model took hold — the "treasury" is under renovation, not yet delivering.
🔴 It is a levered holding company: about €1.62B of net debt sits ahead of the equity, and any break-up value is after that claim.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The most important terminology shift is the "hidden treasury" language itself — that is a company priming the market for a value-crystallization event, whether a partial listing, a stake sale, or a spin of Alarms. The second signal is the strategy pivot in Alarms from volume to quality: raising upfront fees and tightening credit is what a business does when it is being groomed for a valuation event, prioritizing margin and payback over headline client counts. The third, subtler signal is the integration of Cybersecurity into the Security division "as a natural step" — a tidying-up of the structure that makes the three core parts (Security, Cash, Alarms) cleaner to value and separate.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING** on the operating and capital-surfacing axes — profit is inflecting, cash flow turned positive, and management is openly working to close the holding-company discount. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing is this: **the entire case rests on a sum-of-the-parts discount, and the load-bearing catalyst — the December 2026 Alarms investor day — is a soft, non-binding event, not a binding transaction.** There is genuine value in the parts (a market-priced Cash stake plus a credibly growing Alarms business), but nothing yet forces that value to be crystallized, and the group carries real leverage in front of the equity.

On the moat: Prosegur runs a **narrow** moat. Cash-in-transit is a scale-and-density, regulatory-license business — hard to enter, but structurally exposed to the slow secular decline of physical cash usage, which caps its terminal growth. Security (manned guarding) is a low-margin, low-switching-cost, labor-intensive service with little pricing power. Alarms is the best of the three — recurring subscription revenue with real switching costs — but it is the smallest. Returns on capital in the low single digits confirm the moat is narrow, not wide. The relevant secular force — declining cash usage — is **manageable rather than terminal**: it erodes the Cash segment's growth but does not extinguish it, because armored logistics, ATM servicing, and cash management persist for decades even in a digitizing world, and the group is diversifying toward Alarms and technology precisely to offset it.
